messages.subject: Hello there I am wondering about my module iteration.
parts:
Hello there

 I am wondering about my module iteration.

Why my iteration always is 1?

Is it  a problem?

Here is my code and result

pa='wa~s.lat
   wa~s.Height.m.
   wa~s.m.min.T
   wa~s.julianday
   s.m.min.T~s.lat
   s.m.min.T~s.Height.m.
   s.m.min.T~s.julianday
'
fit=cfa(pa,data=df,std.lv=T)
summary(fit, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized=T,rsquare=T)

but, when I use "~~"in s.m.min.T with s.lat.

I have more iteration.

lavaan 0.6.16 ended normally after 1 iteration

I do the process in newest  R and Lavaan version

I am appreciate for any comment or thought.

John

messages.author: f1530326ce101401
messages.subject: Re: Hello there I am wondering about my module iteration.
parts:
Hi John,

My best guess is that your model (as shown in your post) is saturated (or just-identified). This implies that the degrees of freedom = 0 and that the fit of your model is perfect (i.e., the observed and model-implied variance-covariance matrices are identical). When you use '~~' instead of '~' (e.g in  s.m.min.T with s.lat.) your model is not saturated anymore but over-identified. Hence, the estimation procedure will need multiple iterations.

Best wishes,

Jasper

messages.author: bfa43814f6ba1969
messages.subject: Re: Hello there I am wondering about my module iteration.
parts:
Hi,

 

The model is a just-identified recursive model of observed variables. You can estimate it as two regressions and get the same estimates that lavaan gives. This makes estimating this model with sem a bit pointless because sem is more complex but does not provide any advantage.

 

If I remember correctly, lavaan calculates the starting values of regressions between observed variables with regression. If so, the starting values are already the maximum likelihood estimates, and you get convergence in the first iteration.

 

Mikko
